newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank Leumi issues Africa Israel tender.
newsitem.headline: Bank Leumi issues Africa Israel tender.

text.p: Bank Leumi published a new tender on Tuesday for the sale of a controlling stake in the property development company Africa Israel Investments Ltd, this time shorn of its insurance business.

The new tender offer includes the holdings of two Israeli investors, Mordechai Zisser and Eitan Wertheimer, who acquired 14 percent of Africa in August in a bid to block Leumi's plan to spin off Africa's insurance business prior to the tender.
Leumi currently owns 65 percent of the voting rights in Africa Israel.

The two sides are now jointly offering to sell 46.58 percent of equity and 54.2 percent of voting rights in Africa. Bidders are also required to include a put option for an additional five percent. Offers must be filed with the bank by 1100 GMT October 21.

Africa is one of Israel's leading property-development companies and has holdings in hotels, building products and fuel distribution. In September, Africa's shareholders approved Leumi's plan to divest Africa's Leumi Insurance Holdings (LIH) subsidiary by distributing the shares as a dividend.
As a result, Leumi's first Africa tender - published before the spin-off was approved - was cancelled.

Media reports say Leumi will be seeking a minimum price in excess of Africa's market valuation, which as of Monday was $532.5 million. During the summer Africa's share price soared because of an offer by Italian insurer Generali for LIH at an unexpectededly high valuation and because both Leumi and the Zisser-Wertheimer group accumulated Africa shares.
Generali is now on its way to taking control of LIH.

Leumi is required by the government to reduce its holding in Africa to 25 percent as part of bank reform legislation requiring commercial banks to reduce their holdings in non-bank companies. Leumi has to reduce its Africa stake to 20 percent by the end of 1999.
